title: “Prieta, happy in their skin, color, and language”: secondary content area teachers’ navigation of raciolinguistic ideologies in Texas
journal: International Review of Applied Linguistics in Language Teaching
abstract: Abstract This study explores how secondary content-area teachers from raciolinguistically minoritized communities engage with raciolinguistic trauma through participation in a professional development (PD) program at a Hispanic-serving institution in South Texas. Drawing on the framework of raciolinguistic ideologies, we examine data from Project MIRRORS, a graduate-level PD program serving 55 teachers, recruited from two school districts and distributed across three cohorts. Through qualitative data analysis of interviews, digital language stories, identity reflections, and collaborative coaching sessions, we document how participants (a) engaged in intersectional identity work, (b) processed intergenerational and schooling-related linguistic trauma, and (c) reimagined pedagogical practices as acts of healing and resistance. The findings highlight three main areas: engaging in intersectional identity work through PD, reflecting on raciolinguistic trauma, and reclaiming linguistic agency through healing-oriented pedagogy. Teachers’ narratives demonstrate that addressing linguistic racism in TESOL requires attending to the emotional and historical dimensions of language oppression. We argue that trauma-informed teacher education grounded in identity work can foster both individual and collective healing by empowering educators to transform classrooms into spaces of linguistic justice and affirmation.

title: Özbekston Respublikasi misolida parranda grippi epidemiyalarining oziq-ovqat xavfsizligi va iste’mol bozoriga iqtisodiy ta’siri Economic impact of avian influenza epidemics on food security and the consumer market: the case of the Republic of Uzbekistan Экономическое влияние эпидемий птичьего гриппа на продовольственную безопасность и потребительский рынок (на примере Республики Узбекистан)
journal: Partner conferences of the International Scientific Journal Research Focus
abstract: This thesis provides a comprehensive analysis of the origins of Avian Influenza and the biological characteristics of the virus, as well as the adverse impacts of such an epizootic—within the context of the Republic of Uzbekistan—on the national economy, the poultry sector, and price stability in the consumer market. The study examines the economic ripple effects resulting from the spread of the disease, including the contraction of supply, inflationary pressure on market prices, and the subsequent decline in the population’s purchasing power.

title: Who prefers to donate? The impact of global-local identity on individual donations
journal: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
abstract: Purpose The objective of this study is to investigate the effect of global-local identity on individual donations. Design/methodology/approach Using secondary data analyses and two scenario-based online experiments, this study examines the impact of global-local identity on individual donation. Study 1 employs 44,900 individual observations from the sixth wave of the World Values Survey. Studies 2 and 3 collect data from 200 and 360 respondents respectively via an online survey platform (Credamo.com). Findings The results suggest that individuals with a relatively stronger global than local identity orientation are more willing to donate, with the benefit-cost trade-off serving as a significant mediating pathway. Additionally, the association between global-local identity and the benefit-cost trade-off is stronger under far (vs. near) spatial distance. Originality/value This study examines how global-local identity influences individual donation from the perspective of moral rationality and based on regulatory focus theory, and investigates the moderating role of donor-beneficiary spatial distance based on construal level theory, thereby contributing to the literature on global-local identity, individual donation and spatial distance. It also provides practical implications for charitable organizations engaged in global fundraising campaigns.

title: Vitamin D, physical activity and depression: a scoping review of potential combined effects
abstract: Purpose This scoping review aimed to synthesize current evidence on the individual and combined effects of vitamin D status or supplementation and physical activity on depression-related outcomes in adults. Design/methodology/approach A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. PubMed, ScienceDirect and Scopus were searched from database inception through July 2026. Studies were eligible if they included adults and examined vitamin D-related exposure or intervention together with physical activity in relation to depressive symptoms or clinically diagnosed depression. Six eligible studies were included. Findings Vitamin D and physical activity were associated with improvements in depression-related outcomes in some populations, whereas evidence regarding their combined effects was mixed. Potential complementary benefits were more frequently observed among participants with vitamin D deficiency or greater baseline depressive symptom severity. In contrast, studies involving participants with sufficient baseline vitamin D status and low depressive symptom severity generally did not demonstrate additional benefits from combined interventions. Originality/value This review maps the limited evidence on the combined effects of vitamin D and physical activity on depression and highlights potential population and intervention characteristics that may influence these effects.

Sustainability disclosure: transparency or smoke and mirrors?
abstract: Purpose This study aims at advancing the theory of managerial intent and strategic choice with regards to disclosure transparency that companies adopt in sustainability reporting under mandatory disclosure regulations. It investigates whether, and how, corporate performance and governance mechanisms influence the transparency of sustainability reports. Design/methodology/approach The study provides an analysis of sustainability reports published by Italian listed companies, following the implementation of the European Union (EU) Directive 2014/95/EU on sustainability disclosure. Both textual and quantitative analysis are conducted to classify disclosure strategies and to investigate the relationship between transparency levels, corporate performance indicators, and governance structures. Findings The results of this study indicate that firms operating within mandatory disclosure settings do not consistently align the tone of their reporting with their underlying performance and, thus, tone may be used strategically, potentially to obscure unfavourable performance or to manage stakeholder perceptions. Furthermore, the analysis highlights substantial deficiencies in the readability of corporate disclosures. Originality/value This study advances knowledge on the categorization of transparency disclosure strategies. It enhances understanding of the importance of linguistic choices in the reporting of sustainability-related information. Moreover, it provides evidence on the role of managerial disclosure choices within a context of legal obligations. Findings offer practical recommendations for managers, policymakers, and stakeholders seeking to improve the effectiveness and credibility of sustainability disclosures in regulated environments.

title: Structural health monitoring via a knowledge-integration framework: prospective spatial early-warning analysis of the NPL footbridge
abstract: Introduction Condition monitoring of ageing bridges still relies mostly on periodic inspection, which identifies damage only after it has developed. This study seeks to develop prospective monitoring, in which routine sensor data give warning that the structural condition of bridges is changing while there is still time to act. The physical idea we draw on is critical slowing, where a structure approaching a change of state recovers more slowly from small disturbances and becomes more variable. The challenge is to turn this idea into a practical detector that can work on ordinary bridge instrumentation, separate real structural change from seasonal effects, and be evaluated without any information flowing backwards from the evaluation period into the method’s training. Methods We study the National Physical Laboratory (NPL) Footbridge, an instrumented reinforced-concrete cantilever, using its tilt and temperature records for May to October 2012. The entire pipeline is prospective: the environmental correction is a deliberately simple regression fitted on the stable baseline only, chosen after a fuller 17-term model proved too ill-conditioned for reliable extrapolation; the detectors are fitted, calibrated, and evaluated on strictly separated time windows. Results The spatial pattern is clear under this pipeline: all three sensors in the damage zone show a significant rise in variance through the autumn, while all three reference sensors show no significant trend, and the result does not depend on which reference sensor is chosen. A recursive filter provides a complementary early-warning signal through the growing autocorrelation of its innovations, which is robust across sampling rates from 5 minutes to 1 hour. Detectors which carry these physical indicators respond 3 weeks earlier than purely statistical detectors and cover most of the predefined evaluation interval, at the cost of alarms in mid-August whose status—early warning or false alarm—cannot be settled without independent structural evidence; we present both readings. We also openly report that the classical autocorrelation and dominant-eigenvalue indicators are not robust on these data and that no failure time can be extrapolated. Discussion The study is a single-structure proof of concept on a post-damage baseline; the complete code and processed data are provided with the study.

title: STRATEGIES FOR THE SYNERGISTIC DEVELOPMENT OF UNIVERSITY GOVERNANCE SYSTEMS AND STUDENTS’ SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL COMPETENCIES BASED ON MULTIMODAL LEARNING ANALYSIS
abstract: Against the backdrop of higher education governance shifting from “hierarchical control” to “networked co-governance,” students’ social-emotional competencies (SEC) are no longer merely individual psychological variables but have become a core indicator for measuring governance resilience. This paper proposes an “emotion–governance” coupling analysis framework. Utilizing multimodal learning analytics (MLA) technology, it integrates text, speech, facial expressions, body language, interactive behaviors, and physiological signals to construct a dynamic profile of students’ social-emotional competencies, which is then fed back into higher education governance decision-making. Through a quasi-experimental design, the study tracked 1,240 undergraduate students over one academic year. Using a cross-modal attention fusion model and multilevel linear regression, the study found that: 1) The relationship between governance rule density and SEC growth follows an inverted U-shape (inflection point λ = 0.62); 2) The emotional bond between faculty and students significantly promotes SEC development through two pathways: “emotional support → relational skills” and “academic efficacy → self-management” (β = 0.34, p < 0.01); 3) A multimodal early warning mechanism increased the identification and recall rate of high-risk students to 86.7%, representing a 19.2% improvement over a single-modal approach. Based on these findings, this paper proposes the “Adaptive Emotional Governance Network” model, providing an actionable pathway for the synergistic evolution of university governance and student development.
